checker_requirements.pattern_description: Match calls to `cancel_delayed_work` followed by `tb_tunnel_put` in `tb_dp_dprx_stop`.  Modify the code to put tb_tunnel_put into `tb_dp_dprx_stop` only if cancel_delayed_work returns true. Also, find tb_tunnel_put at the end of `tb_dp_dprx_work`.

vulnerable.description: The code has a use-after-free vulnerability.  `tb_tunnel` is being freed by `tb_tunnel_put` while the delayed work item `tunnel->dprx_work` is still running, leading to a use-after-free in `tb_dp_dprx_work`. The issue is caused by a race condition where `cancel_delayed_work()` in `tb_dp_dprx_stop` does not guarantee the completion of the worker function and may cause `tb_tunnel` to be freed before `tb_dp_dprx_work` is completed.  `tb_dp_dprx_work` will dereference the freed `tb_tunnel`.
key_indicators: Access to `tunnel` within `tb_dp_dprx_work` after it has been potentially freed.
vulnerable.exploitability: The vulnerability is exploitable by triggering the race condition where tb_dp_dprx_work is running at the same time tb_dp_dprx_stop is called which will release the memory. This could lead to a crash or potentially arbitrary code execution if memory is reallocated and controlled.

fixed.description: The fix adds a check to see if `cancel_delayed_work` returns true (work pending). If true, then `tb_tunnel_put` is called in `tb_dp_dprx_stop`, otherwise the tb_tunnel_put is called in `tb_dp_dprx_work` after the callback has been executed.
required_checks: Conditionally call `tb_tunnel_put(tunnel)` in `tb_dp_dprx_stop` based on the return value of `cancel_delayed_work`.
fixed.protection_mechanism: Reference counting to ensure the lifetime of tb_tunnel is properly managed in the presence of delayed work.

context.impact: Crash, or potentially arbitrary code execution if the freed memory is reused and controlled.
context.exploitability: The vulnerability is exploitable by triggering the race condition where tb_dp_dprx_work is running at the same time tb_dp_dprx_stop is called which will release the memory. This could lead to a crash or potentially arbitrary code execution if memory is reallocated and controlled.
